newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock markets to fall - brokers.
newsitem.headline: China stock markets to fall - brokers.

text.p: China's stock markets are expected to fall on Monday in the wake of the strong announcement from Beijing carried by all the national media saying the markets have become over-speculative, brokers said.
The majority of stocks on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges are likely to fall to the 10 percent limit on movements imposed late on Friday, they said.
But they said the impact on the foreign exchange B shares is likely to be smaller than on the domestic A share markets.

"Almost all stocks are expected to fall to the limit on the opening," said a broker at a Chinese brokerage. "No one knows how far down the market will go so there will be very few people willing to buy."

But the stock indices are not expected to fall as far as 10 percent, because not all stocks will fall to that point, and B shares are likely to be less affected than A shares, foreign and local brokers said.
"I think the measures are focused on A shares rather than B shares," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage in Shanghai. "But a lot of B shares will also hit the 10 percent limit."

Monday's People's Daily, in an editorial carried in all major newspapers, said the country's stock markets were overheating on widespread speculation and warned of a crash similar to the great Wall Street collapse of 1929.
The newspaper, the official mouthpiece of the ruling Chinese Communist Party, warned that "the government... will never step in to help the markets when they slump."

Last Friday, the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges announced that they were imposing a limit of 10 percent on daily movements for individual stocks with effect from Monday to stop extraordinary price movements.
That move was clearly intended to forestall a possible crash on Monday following the People's Daily policy announcement.
"Recent skyrocketing has been very abnormal and irrational," the commentary said. "We must further check excessive speculation. "We must strengthen supervision and regulation."
